propositions: The registry generator recognises only os.environ.get, os.environ[...] subscript, and os.getenv forms, silently skipping unrecognised accessor methods like pop and setdefault, causing environment variables read via those forms to be absent from docs/env-vars.md without warning.

Changing os.environ.get(...) to os.environ.pop(...) preserves the read behaviour but drops the variable from the generated registry, violating the invariant that a new env-var read cannot ship undocumented.

The CI drift gate test_generators_not_stale_and_include_new_keys catches stale registry only in the full suite, not in make lint, creating asymmetry between local and CI verdicts and delaying feedback to contributors.

The fix extends KEY_BEARING to include get, pop, setdefault, and __getitem__, classifies all other os.environ attributes as bulk operations (copy, items, keys, values, etc.), and raises UnrecognisedEnvironAccess for any accessor method not in either set, converting silent omission to a loud build failure.

Adding python scripts/gen_env_registry.py --check to the make lint target aligns local and CI signals, so a stale or incomplete registry now fails lint immediately instead of only appearing in the full suite.
